added_detail.reason: copper ores and concentrates, the mining stage of grid copper.

refined copper cathodes, the refining stage of grid copper and the feedstock of the wire rod in Electric Grid Midstream (7408.11). Other unwrought refined copper (7403.12/13/19: wire-bars, billets, other cast shapes; 5% of refined unwrought copper trade, leaders swinging from COD to PAK between 2020 and 2023) and copper waste and scrap (7404, exported by scrap generators) are left out.

unwrought aluminium alloys: smelters cast much of their output as alloy billet and slab (leaders ARE, CAN, NOR, MYS, BHR). Aluminium waste and scrap (7602) is left out: its exporters are scrap generators (USA, DEU), not suppliers of metal.
unwrought aluminium, not alloyed: primary smelter metal (conductor grades are unalloyed).
aluminium oxide (alumina), the refining stage of grid aluminium; smelting takes most of it.
unrefined copper and copper anodes (blister), the smelting stage of grid copper.
bauxite, the mining stage of grid aluminium.

natural uranium and its compounds, the heading under which most uranium ore concentrate is shipped (U3O8, yellowcake: Kazakhstan, Canada, Uzbekistan). An ore concentrate is a raw material, so the code sits Upstream (the master's stage rule) and uranium miners no longer rank as fuel-cycle manufacturers; Nuclear Midstream keeps enriched uranium (2844.20), spent fuel (2844.50) and the reactor and steam-plant hardware.
a battery mineral shared with Batteries Upstream (the code counts fully in both cells).

Electric Vehicles Upstream is the battery minerals and the magnet rare earths of the traction motor. The battery minerals are Batteries Upstream's ores and concentrates, shared with that cell (each code counts fully in both, as the cells and packs both Midstreams hold); the recycling codes stay in Batteries only. Refined chemicals and intermediates stay in Batteries Midstream, so lithium carbonate (Chile), nickel matte and mixed hydroxide (Indonesia) and cobalt hydroxide (DR Congo) are not in this cell, and copper is in Electric Grid Upstream only.
a battery mineral shared with Batteries Upstream (the code counts fully in both cells).
silicon with less than 99.99% Si, i.e. metallurgical-grade silicon metal, the feedstock of polysilicon (2804.61, Solar Midstream).

compounds of rare-earth metals (oxides, carbonates, chlorides). The HS has no ore code for bastnaesite or ion-adsorption clays, so mined concentrates and mixed carbonates trade here (Myanmar, the United States, Laos) beside the separated oxides (China, Malaysia, Japan): the heading is the rare-earth raw material, Upstream as copper cathode is in Electric Grid Upstream, and Midstream starts at the permanent magnet (8505.11). Cerium compounds (2846.10: polishing powders and catalysts, not magnet rare earths) are left out.

compounds of rare-earth metals (oxides, carbonates, chlorides). The HS has no ore code for bastnaesite or ion-adsorption clays, so mined concentrates and mixed carbonates trade here (Myanmar, the United States, Laos) beside the separated oxides (China, Malaysia, Japan): the heading is the rare-earth raw material, Upstream as copper cathode is in Electric Grid Upstream, and Midstream starts at the permanent magnet (8505.11). Cerium compounds (2846.10: polishing powders and catalysts, not magnet rare earths) are left out.

unwrought gallium, germanium and indium (with niobium and vanadium), their powders and scrap: the semiconductor industry's minor metals as primary metal, Upstream by the master's stage rule; Midstream keeps polysilicon, germanium oxides, wafers and the wrought articles (8112.99). Semiconductors is not a headline technology: the cell is descriptive and its HHI index is placed against the headline cells. Left out: silicon metal (2804.69, in Solar Upstream; electronics take a few percent of it), arsenic (2804.80: lead alloys lead its use), rare gases (2804.29: helium leads its trade), fluorspar (2529.21/22: hydrofluoric acid for refrigerants and aluminium) and high-purity quartz (no code of its own).

uranium ores and concentrates, the mining stage of nuclear fuel; Namibia, Australia, Niger and Canada file their concentrate here, others under 2844.10. Thorium ores (2612.20) are left out of Nuclear: there is no commercial thorium fuel cycle, and the heading's trade is monazite sold for its rare earths (in Wind and Electric Vehicles Upstream). 11.0% of the Comtrade 2024 Nuclear Upstream basket (Atlas 2023: 10.7%)

natural graphite powder and flakes, the anode raw material; a battery mineral shared with Batteries Upstream (the code counts fully in both cells). 2.8% of the Comtrade 2024 Electric Vehicles Upstream basket (Atlas 2023: 1.7%)

rare-earth metals, scandium and yttrium, reduced from the separated oxides as the feedstock of magnet alloys (China, Thailand, Viet Nam, Japan): the metallic form of the magnet rare earths, Upstream with their compounds.

rare-earth metals, scandium and yttrium, reduced from the separated oxides as the feedstock of magnet alloys (China, Thailand, Viet Nam, Japan): the metallic form of the magnet rare earths, Upstream with their compounds.

thorium ores and concentrates, the HS heading of monazite, a rare-earth phosphate ore from heavy-mineral sands (Nigeria, Thailand, Madagascar) sold to separators for its neodymium and praseodymium; its thorium has no commercial use, so the code is not in Nuclear. 0.2% of the Comtrade 2024 Electric Vehicles Upstream basket (Atlas 2023: 0.5%)
